newsitem.title: UK: Russian Duma budget chief paints rosy picture.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma budget chief paints rosy picture.

text.p: The Russian Duma's Budget Committee Chairman, Mikhail Zadornov, painted an optimistic picture of the country's economy on Thursday but said that tax collection, wage arrears and internal debts remained critical problems.

"Economic prospects for 1997 will reflect two factors, the momentum of the last two or three years and the actions of the new government, which will show in the second half of the year," he said during a conference here.
He said that interest rates fell from 200 percent to 48 percent last year, and are now down to 42 percent, and added that commercial banks are also bringing down their rates.
Although inflation is tending to rise, he said this was common at the beginning of the year and it should fall to 1 percent a month shortly, down from an annual 23 percent last year.
And he added that the exchange rate is stable, the Central Bank holds foreign currency reserves of $15 billion and rising, as well as 300 tonnes of gold.

But despite apparently healthy signs, investment fell by 18 percent last year and no change is visible from this downward spiral in the first two months of this year. And revenue collection remains disastrously low, he added.
"In the last year and a half, the government has only been able to bring in 70 percent of what it expected in revenue, so the government has become a debtor."
This has made the central government one of the biggest non-payers of arrears, he added.
"Arrears are growing three times faster than inflation, so the financial position of every enterprise has worsened," he said. And inter-enterprise debt is getting worse, not better.
"It may look as if we have a favourable trend, but no. Last year's figures, even for the main exports like oil, gas, metals and timber were all worse than in 1995."
He said that wage arrears now total 10 trillion roubles ($1.8 billion), with wages on average two months in arrears. And pension arrears total 16 trillion roubles.
The Central Bank's policy is likely to remain unchanged and the macroeconomic situation should improve further, he said.

Inflation should reach 15 percent this year, and the yield on government securities should be no higher than 25 percent by the end of the year, allowing interest rates to be cut further. But he doubted the government's expected growth rate of two percent was possible, adding that zero or negative growth was Unpaid taxes now total 70 trillion roubles, he said, with fines for non-payment already reaching 100 trillion roubles. But he said that work has at last started on reforming the tax code, and added that the legislative and executive branches of government agree that 1997 will be a year of far reaching changes to the tax system.

Zadornov said that all these changes and others, including laws on foreign investments and bankruptcy, will depend on the restructuring of the government now under way. He raised concerns over the restructuring, although he said the measures, though necessary, were deeply unpopular and would have no political support.
"But governments in Russia are always unpopular, it's an endemic thing," he added.
-- Sebastian Alison, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 6412 ($ = 5697 Russian Roubles)
